title: Platform lab governance and synthetic workload seeding policy
author: Marina Chen
content:
Summary

This page defines the governance model, access controls, and the standardized policy for seeding synthetic workloads and datasets into Redwood platform lab environments. The goal is to enable reliable, repeatable experimentation for platform engineering (capacity planning, degradation testing, preflight rollouts, and telemetry validation) while limiting cost, protecting customer data, and ensuring observability parity with production.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood-managed lab clusters and sandbox tenants used by platform, infra, and runtime teams.
- Covers synthetic dataset generation, workload replay seeding, telemetry labeling, cost accounting, and incident/runbook expectations.
- Excludes customer-owned air-gapped private deployments; those are governed by eng-private-deployments policies.

Goals and guiding principles

1. Safety-first: No real customer PII or telemetry is used unless explicitly approved by Security & Compliance and anonymized.
2. Reproducibility: Workloads must be seedable and deterministic where practical; tests should be runnable by operators and CI.
3. Observability parity: Telemetry and tracing must be emitted using the same schemas and SLI hooks as prod.
4. Cost awareness: Synthetic campaigns must include budget caps and cost owners; platform lab credit system enforces limits.
5. Low cognitive load for operators: Provide templated scripts, dashboards, and automated cleanup.

Lab environment types (definitions)

- Sandbox (ephemeral): Short-lived, isolated namespaces for developer experiments. No SLA. Max lifetime: 48 hours unless extended.
- Integration (staging-like): Longer-lived environments for multi-service integration with representative telemetry. Max lifetime: 30 days.
- Stress-grid (capacity): Dedicated pools for load tests at scale; scheduled and billed to test owners.

Access and RBAC

- Roles:
  - lab-operator: create/tear down sandboxes, schedule stress-grid tests.
  - lab-engineer: run seeded workloads and access telemetry dashboards.
  - lab-admin: manage quotas and cost caps.
- Onboarding: Access requires a valid JIRA ticket describing the experiment, owner, estimated cost, and retention window. The lab-admin grants roles after review.
- Approvals: Stress-grid tests > 50% of a regional capacity require pre-approval from Capacity Planning and SRE.

Synthetic dataset seeding policy

1. Allowed sources:
   - Generated synthetic text using Redwood synthetic-generator (see Appendix A)
   - Anonymized and consented public datasets (CC0 or similarly permissive)
2. Disallowed sources:
   - Production PII or un-anonymized customer logs without a legal-approved data-sharing agreement
3. Labeling and provenance:
   - Every seeded dataset must include a metadata file (seed-manifest.json) with fields: name, seed_id, generator_version, created_by, created_at, retained_until, and allowed_use_cases.
   - Example manifest (stringified JSON) to include in artifacts:
   {"name": "conversational-dialogue-202502", "seed_id": "lab-gn-2025-02-12", "generator_version": "v1.3.0", "created_by": "marina.chen@redwood.ai", "created_at": "2025-02-12T16:22:00Z", "retained_until": "2025-03-12", "allowed_use_cases": ["runtime-benchmark", "kv-cache-warmup"]}
4. Retention:
   - Sandbox datasets: auto-deleted after environment teardown.
   - Integration datasets: default retention 30 days; expiration embedded in seed-manifest triggers automatic cleanup.
   - Stress-grid artifacts (logs/artillery traces): retained 90 days for postmortem analysis.

Synthetic workload generation and seeding recipes

- Supported generators:
  - redwood-synth-gen (text/dialogue/short-prompt families)
  - replay-builder (replays of captured production-like sequences but mapped to synthetic IDs)
- Standard seeding workflow (recommended):
  1. Create seed-manifest and commit to team lab artifact bucket.
  2. Register workload in Lab Orchestration (lab-orch) with tags: owner, budget_center, SLI_profile, region.
  3. Dry-run at 1% scale to validate telemetry and cleanup hooks.
  4. Execute scaled runs.
  5. Post-run: trigger artifact collection and retention policy; mark run as complete in JIRA.

Example command snippets

- Create a seed manifest (CLI):
  labctl seed create --name conversational-dialogue-202502 --generator redwood-synth-gen:v1.3.0 --retention 30d --owner marina.chen@redwood.ai

- Register workload with orchestration:
  labctl run register --seed-id lab-gn-2025-02-12 --profile latency-sensitive --budget 3000 --region us-west-2

- Dry-run execution (1%):
  labctl run execute --id run-4732 --scale 0.01 --notify-on-failure --trace-sample-rate 1/1000

Telemetry, labeling, and observability requirements

- Telemetry alignment:
  - Use studio.sli.* metric keys for experiments to ensure dashboards reuse production SLI aggregations.
  - Trace spans must contain: service, workload.seed_id, experiment.run_id, and operator.persona tags.
- Dashboards:
  - Every experiment must instantiate a dashboard from the lab-dashboard-template. Required panels: request latency p50/p95/p99, token-cost per minute, error-rate by class, KV cache hit ratio, and resource contention heatmap.
- Synthetic-run tagging (minimum): [lab:true, seed_id:<seed>, run_id:<id>, owner:<email>]

Cost, budgeting and chargeback

- Budgets are declared at registration. The lab billing job enforces soft caps (alerts) at 80% and hard caps (throttle) at 100%.
- Owners must assign a GraphCost center tag for chargeback.
- Emergency overrun: operator must open pg-ticket with justification; finance will reconcile within 7 business days.

Runbook: lab incident and runaway workload procedure

1. Symptoms:
  - Unexpectedly high QPS or GPU utilization for a seeded workload.
  - Spike in token-cost or steady SLI burn not aligned with test plan.
2. Immediate actions (first 15 minutes):
  a. lab-operator pauses the run: labctl run pause --id <run_id>.
  b. Capture pre-pause snapshot: labctl run snapshot --id <run_id> --output /tmp/run-snapshot.tgz.
  c. Notify stakeholders: #platform-ops, SRE duty, and capacity-planning.
3. Investigation (15–90 minutes):
  - Check seed-manifest and generator_version for known divergence.
  - Review telemetry panels and recent config rollouts.
  - If cost > 150% of estimate, escalate to lab-admin for emergency tear-down.
4. Recovery and lessons:
  - If workload resumed successfully after config fix, annotate JIRA run ticket and schedule postmortem within 7 days.
  - If the run caused cross-tenant degradation, execute tenancy-fairing rollbacks and notify customers per incident playbook.

Compliance and data handling

- All synthetic datasets must be validated by Data Privacy Automation (DPA) pipelines before lab registration.
- When an experiment requires production-derived data (rare), a Data Use Agreement (DUA) is required and Security must run an approval check.

Onboarding checklist for new lab experiments

1. Create JIRA experiment ticket with: owner, cost estimate, retention, and SLI profile.
2. Prepare seed-manifest and link to artifact bucket.
3. Run 1% dry-run and attach artifacts to JIRA.
4. Grant temporary lab role if needed and set budget tag.
5. Schedule run window and notify platform-observability channel.

Operational ownership and review cadence

- Owners: experiment owner (day-to-day), lab-admin (quota/cost), SRE (safety & escalation), Capacity Planning (stress-grid approvals).
- Review cadence:
  - Monthly: lab-admin reviews active experiments and cost report.
  - Quarterly: platform leadership reviews lab-runbook incidents and updates templates.

Appendix A: Minimal synthetic generator config example

# minimal config (YAML)
generator:
  name: redwood-synth-gen
  version: v1.3.0
  families:
    - dialogue
    - short_prompt
  seed: 20250212
  retain_samples: 100000

- lab-dashboard-template: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/lab-dashboard-template
- seed-manifest template: s3://redwood-lab-artifacts/templates/seed-manifest.json
- labctl CLI docs: /internal-docs/labctl/README

Contact and feedback

If you have suggestions or need exceptions, open a ticket with subject: [LAB-POLICY-EXCEPTION] and tag lab-admin.
